opportunities.title: Rebuild the front door: recover the DNS zone, publish a small AI-readable site, claim and correct the Google Business Profile, and fix the parked email domain
opportunities.problem: The firm has no working owned web presence at all. rosedeb.com is paid up through June 2027 but its Cloudflare nameservers now REFUSE queries, so every page (including the old 'contact me online' intake path) is unreachable; the only Google listing still points customers at that dead domain, is unclaimed, and shows no hours; and the email domain published on the current court roster, darosepc.com, serves a parked ad page. A prospective client who searches her name today lands on a directory or a browser error, and the one channel left is a phone number printed in a court PDF.
evidence: Google Public DNS returns status 2 for rosedeb.com, comment 'Name servers refused query (lame delegation?)', with rcode=REFUSED from all six Cloudflare nameservers (https://dns.google/resolve?name=rosedeb.com&type=A)

Registry record: created 2003-06-04, expires 2027-06-04, 'last changed' 2026-06-05, registrar Register.com, nameservers CHIP/NELLY.NS.CLOUDFLARE.COM - so the registration was not lost; the zone was detached (inference: deliberate switch-off, four days after the last HTTP 200 archive capture) (https://rdap.verisign.com/com/v1/domain/rosedeb.com)

Google Business Profile 'Deborah Rose PC' at 850 Carolier Ln is unclaimed ('Claim this business'), lists no hours ('Add hours') and its website field still points at rosedeb.com (https://www.google.com/maps/place/Deborah+Rose+PC/@40.4622146,-74.4540979,17z)
The published email domain darosepc.com resolves to an ad-framed parked page rather than any firm content (https://darosepc.com/)

Last archived home page (1 June 2026) offered a free initial consultation by phone or 'contact me online', several payment-plan options, and carried LocalBusiness schema whose geo coordinates pointed to North Carolina with hours of 08:00-08:00 (http://web.archive.org/web/20260601225044/https://www.rosedeb.com/)

The current Middlesex family-law mediator roster publishes her firm, address, phone, fax, email and $300/hour rate - i.e. the firm's key facts now live only in a court PDF, not on any page she controls (https://njj-aocmedia-prod-general-purpose.s3.amazonaws.com/rosters/family-law/middlesex.pdf)
opportunities.agent_design: Fix the substrate first, then put a thin agent layer on it. (1) Recover control of the DNS zone at Register.com/Cloudflare and re-point rosedeb.com (or a clean new domain) at a fast five-page static site: attorney profile, practice areas, mediation offer with the published $300/hour rate, service area (North Brunswick plus the 20+ towns on the old contact page), contact. (2) Claim the Google Business Profile, set real hours, correct the website field and service area, and link the reviews that already exist on Avvo/Lawyers.com. (3) Publish machine-readable facts - attorney, Certified Matrimonial Attorney status, practice areas, hours, phone, service area - as schema.org LegalService so search and AI assistants can read and cite them instead of stale indexed titles. (4) Behind the form, a consultation-request agent replies in English/Spanish, captures matter type and both parties' names for a conflict check, and queues a callback or a calendar slot; the attorney approves every new matter, engagement letter and fee quote. No automatic fee quotes, no automatic engagement. (5) Separately confirm mail routing at darosepc.com so the court-published address does not silently bounce.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: A site builder cannot re-delegate a detached DNS zone on a domain that is already paid for, cannot claim and correct a listing that has been unclaimed for years, and will not produce the structured data and answer-shaped content that AI assistants and Google actually read. The intake step is not a contact form: it is a bilingual, conflict-aware triage agent with a human approval gate, and it touches prospective-client data, so it needs a confidentiality-preserving configuration rather than a $20/month form widget.

impact_estimate.range: No new revenue assumed from the site itself. If a working front door plus a claimed listing recovers 1-2 additional booked mediation or consultation hours a month at her published $300/hour, that is roughly $300-$600/month ($3.6k-$7.2k/year) - an inference, not a measurement. Secondary, unquantified: removes the dead-link and 'no hours' defects on the only listing customers still find, and removes the risk that the email address published on the court roster is undeliverable.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Lost-inquiry volume is unobservable (no analytics on a dead site, no call tracking). The $300/hour figure is her roster-published mediation rate, and only part of her work is mediation, so the same rate is an upper bound for consultation time. If the practice is already near a solo's capacity - or is being wound down into her Of Counsel role at The Busch Law Group - the gain is avoided non-billable phone time rather than new fees.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 2 weeks: regain DNS control and stand up a five-page site with a consultation-request form; claim the Google Business Profile and fix hours, website field and service area; publish LegalService schema and an AI-assistant-readable facts block; verify mail routing at darosepc.com; deliver a before/after check that the domain resolves, the form delivers, and the listing no longer points at a dead host.

opportunities.title: Bilingual 24/7 intake, conflict-screen and consultation-booking agent on top of the restored front door
opportunities.problem: With the site dark and no booking tool, every enquiry is a phone call answered (or missed) by the attorney personally, and the only online 'contact' paths left are third-party directory forms that route the lead to the directory rather than the firm. Family-law enquiries are time-critical - domestic violence restraining orders, custody, support - and her own bio notes frequent representation of Spanish-speaking clients, so a phone-only, business-hours, English-first intake is a poor fit for the demand she actually serves.
evidence: The only firm-controlled channels on the current roster are phone (732) 821-3055 and fax (732) 821-8857; no online intake, booking or quote path exists anywhere (https://njj-aocmedia-prod-general-purpose.s3.amazonaws.com/rosters/family-law/middlesex.pdf)

Before the outage, intake ran through a free-consultation click-to-call block and a 'contact me online' page; neither is reachable now (http://web.archive.org/web/20260601225044/https://www.rosedeb.com/)

Even the archived site had no case-management portal, document upload, calendar or payment page - client work is coordinated by phone, fax and email (http://web.archive.org/web/20260601225044/https://www.rosedeb.com/contact-us/)

Lawyers.com provides its own 'Email Deborah' contact form, which routes the enquiry to the directory rather than the firm (https://www.lawyers.com/north-brunswick/new-jersey/deborah-a-rose-1086276-a/)
Her Busch Law Group bio states she frequently represents Spanish-speaking clients, and the Lawyers.com profile lists Spanish among languages (https://www.buschlawgroup.com/deborah-a-rose/)

Automated intake triage is technically feasible at this volume: an ensemble of inexpensive models plus auto-generated follow-up questions reached 97.37% hits@2 in routing 419 real queries to a nonprofit lawyer referral service (academic conference paper, JURIX 2025) (https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.07170)

Proxy evidence for intake/correspondence throughput: staggered rollout of generative AI to 5,179 customer-support agents raised issues resolved per hour by 14% on average, with larger gains for less-experienced workers (peer-reviewed, NBER Working Paper 31161; Quarterly Journal of Economics 140(2), 2025) - not a law-firm study (https://www.nber.org/papers/w31161)
opportunities.agent_design: A voice plus web/email intake agent in English and Spanish. Triggers: an inbound call to a ported VoIP number (with after-hours and missed-call fallback), the site's consultation form, or a directory email. It transcribes and summarises the enquiry, classifies the matter (divorce, custody/support, DV restraining order, adoption, mediation, guardian ad litem appointment), records both parties' names for a conflict screen against a client/matter list the attorney maintains, checks county/jurisdiction and any imminent deadline, then offers three consultation slots from her calendar and sends a confirmation with a 'what to bring' checklist. Exceptions route to the attorney by SMS/email with a one-screen brief: existing clients, anything that reads as an emergency restraining-order situation, a possible conflict, fee or payment-plan questions, and anything the classifier is unsure about. The attorney approves every new matter, engagement letter and fee quote; nothing is auto-accepted, and every transcript, decision and approval is logged so supervision under N.J. RPC 1.1/5.3 is auditable.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: It has to answer a live phone line, work in Spanish, classify a legal problem well enough to route it, run a conflict check against matter records, write to a calendar and mail, and escalate emergencies to a human on a rule the firm defines. It also stores prospective-client confidences, so it needs a confidentiality-preserving vendor arrangement and per-matter access control under R.P.C. 1.6 rather than a consumer chatbot. A subscription FAQ bot does no integration, no conflict screening and leaves no audit trail.

impact_estimate.range: Roughly 120-300 attorney hours a year returned from call screening, message taking and consult scheduling, worth about $9,000-$23,000 at the ~$78/hour New Jersey lawyer median, plus a throughput gain in the low-to-mid teens of percent on routine correspondence (proxy from the support-agent study). Assumes 4-6 enquiries handled per business day at 8-15 minutes each and that she currently handles them herself - inferred, not measured.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Call volume, current answer rate and whether any assistant exists are all unobserved (no site, no job postings, no published hours), so the hours figure is an order-of-magnitude estimate. The saving is attorney time, not new revenue; it converts to margin only through extra matter capacity or reduced write-downs. If the practice is winding down toward Of Counsel work at The Busch Law Group, the ceiling is materially lower.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 3 weeks: one VoIP number and one web form; top four matter types plus mediation; English/Spanish; conflict list loaded from a spreadsheet she maintains; booking into her existing calendar; human-approval queue for new matters; measured against 30 real or reconstructed enquiries scored on the same routing decision she would have made, with an emergency-escalation test plan she signs off before go-live.

opportunities.title: Private matter-file knowledge agent that answers client status questions and drafts from her own briefs, letters and precedents
opportunities.problem: Her differentiator is one-on-one responsiveness - the firm was deliberately kept small, and reviewers praise being kept informed and reachable - but with no document management system, no portal and files moving by phone, fax and email, every status answer, discovery chase and first draft consumes attorney hours. The thing clients rate her for is exactly the thing that does not scale, and it competes with court time and the mediation line.
evidence: Archived home page: the firm is deliberately kept small because 'every client deserves one-on-one attention from their attorney', with questions answered 'as promptly as possible' (http://web.archive.org/web/20260601225044/https://www.rosedeb.com/)

Reviewers reward exactly that: Lawyers.com reviewers stress being kept informed and reachable (communication 4.8, responsiveness 5.0 across four reviews), and the 16 Avvo reviews praise responsiveness and availability (https://www.lawyers.com/north-brunswick/new-jersey/deborah-a-rose-1086276-a/)

No case-management portal, document upload, calendar or payment page appears in the archived site, and nothing suggests a document management system (http://web.archive.org/web/20260601225044/https://www.rosedeb.com/contact-us/)

There is substantive precedent material to ground drafts in: five published Appellate Division decisions cited as representative matters, including Platt v. Platt (2006) (https://www.lawyers.com/north-brunswick/new-jersey/deborah-a-rose-1086276-a/)

Hallucination evidence makes citation verification mandatory: ChatGPT-4 produced legal hallucinations about 58% of the time on verifiable federal case questions (peer-reviewed, Journal of Legal Analysis 16(1), 2024) (https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.01301)
Even RAG-based legal research tools hallucinated between 17% and 33% of the time in the first preregistered evaluation (academic working paper, not peer-reviewed) (https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.20362)

Confidentiality bounds the design: client files and settlement communications cannot go into consumer LLM endpoints without a confidentiality-preserving contract, and the lawyer remains responsible for supervising the work (industry brief constraint set, N.J. R.P.C. 1.6/5.3, framed from domain knowledge and not re-fetched)
opportunities.agent_design: A single-tenant, zero-retention knowledge agent over her own corpus: matter files, engagement letters and payment-plan terms, prior briefs and correspondence, the five published appellate decisions, and her mediation/guardian ad litem and Domestic Violence Pilot protocols. Access is per-matter; the vendor trains on nothing and keeps no prompt logs; deployment is in a private tenant or on a machine in the office. Two jobs. (a) Internal: 'what is outstanding in this matter', 'draft the status update from these three documents', 'summarise this Case Information Statement against the last one', 'pull the argument we used on this issue in the prior brief' - each answer returns quoted passages with file and page. (b) Client-facing: draft replies and periodic status notes queued for her approval, never sent automatically. A citation-verification step checks every quoted authority against the source file and blocks any claim without a supporting passage before output. Human approval sits on every outbound message and every filing-bound draft.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: The corpus is privileged client data spanning decades, so it cannot be pasted into a consumer chatbot; it needs per-matter access control, no-training terms, immutable logs for supervision, and retrieval tuned to her own documents rather than the open web - plus mandatory citation checking, which the measured hallucination rates make non-optional. That is a permissioned private deployment with a verification harness, not a subscription.

impact_estimate.range: Roughly 100-200 attorney hours a year on status updates, discovery chasing and first-draft correspondence, worth about $7,800-$15,600 at the ~$78/hour New Jersey lawyer median. No revenue uplift assumed; the real payoff is that responsiveness stops competing with court and mediation hours.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Assumes she writes these herself today and that 2-4 hours a week go to them - inferred from the solo, no-staff, no-portal structure, not observed. Corpus state is unknown: 40 years of files may be largely paper, in which case scanning and OCR could dominate the pilot and eat the first months of benefit. Savings are attorney time, not fees.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 3-4 weeks: ingest 3 closed matters, 1 open matter and her published appellate decisions; 50 test questions scored against her own answers for correctness and citation fidelity; a citation-verification harness that blocks unsupported claims; private/zero-retention deployment with per-matter permissions; and a short written verdict on how much of her archive is digitised enough to be worth loading.

lead_score.rationale: Pain is verified from primary sources rather than inferred: the domain's nameservers actively REFUSE queries while the registration is paid to June 2027, the archive-verified last live capture is 1 June 2026 against a registry change on 5 June 2026, the unclaimed Google listing still sends customers to that host with no hours shown, and the email domain on the current court roster is a parked ad page. That is a front-door failure, so capability G leads. Fit is high because the same broken front door forces the other two opportunities into the A/C band the consultancy already builds: no online intake, no portal, no document system, all on one attorney. Ability to pay is the limiter: one attorney, no job postings, no visible IT spend, and a plausible consolidation into her Of Counsel role at The Busch Law Group, so budget may be small or the practice may be winding down; matter volume and current answer rate are also unobserved. Ease is good on the G work (a two-week DNS/site/listing fix) but the buyer is only reachable by phone or at the office, which slows everything. Strategic value is real but not top-tier: 'solo/small firm front door recovery plus intake agent' is repeatable across hundreds of New Jersey family-law practices whose sites decay exactly this way. No avenues.json was supplied and there is no physical operation to instrument - the only physical asset is leased suite space in a 1975 multi-tenant office building, with no inventory, equipment, dock, kitchen or fleet - so no capability E opportunity was proposed; a camera or sensor deployment here would be surveillance of a law office with no operational payoff.

best_evidence_signal: rosedeb.com returns SERVFAIL with 'Name servers refused query (lame delegation?)' - the DNS zone is detached even though the domain is paid to 2027 - while the unclaimed Google Business Profile still points customers at it (https://dns.google/resolve?name=rosedeb.com&type=A)
suggested_channel: walk-in (the office at 850 Carolier Ln is the reliable route; there is no working website and the published email domain is parked, so phone 732-821-3055 is the fallback)
